scope: Brief educational muscle-function summaries; not individualized medical advice.

provenance.method: Original concise source-supported summaries prepared with AI assistance; no copied textbook passages
provenance.training_use: Excluded from neural training. Model uses only user-supplied exercise names and source target labels.
provenance.attribution: Anatomy references: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, Betts et al. Access for free at https://openstax.org/books/anatomy-and-physiology-2e/pages/1-introduction

priority.title: Simao et al. 2010: Influence of Exercise Order

muscles.function: Abdominal muscles help bend, rotate and stabilize the trunk; different muscles perform different actions.
Pectoralis major brings the upper arm forward and across the chest.
Biceps bends the elbow and turns the forearm palm-up.
Deltoid raises the arm; its front and back portions also move the arm forward and backward.
Latissimus dorsi pulls the upper arm back and toward the body.
This broad region includes muscles that position and stabilize the shoulder blades, such as the rhomboids.
Trapezius helps position the shoulder blades; actions differ across its upper, middle and lower portions.
Forearm muscles move the wrist and fingers; some rotate the forearm.
Serratus anterior moves the shoulder blade forward around the rib cage.
Levator scapulae raises the shoulder blade.
Gluteus maximus extends the hip. Gluteus medius and minimus move the thigh outward and help stabilize the pelvis.
Quadriceps straighten the knee. Rectus femoris also helps bend the hip.
Hamstrings bend the knee; most also extend the hip.
Gastrocnemius and soleus point the foot downward at the ankle; gastrocnemius also assists knee bending.
Hip adductors bring the thigh toward the midline.
Hip abductors move the thigh away from the midline.
The spine is a body structure, not a muscle. Nearby back muscles help extend and stabilize the trunk.
This source category refers to conditioning, not a single skeletal muscle. Exercise targets alone do not specify a training dose.

ordering.principle: After preparation, place exercises most important to the session goal early. There is no universal first exercise or rule that a larger muscle must always come first.

steps.instruction: Check readiness and apply the independent safety rules before training.
Use easy general movement, relevant movement rehearsal and gradual warm-up sets for the planned exercises.
Perform the main goal-focused work while fresh. Technical or power work requires appropriate skill and a reviewed plan.
Follow with the remaining planned exercises and accessories; avoid unnecessary pre-fatigue of a priority exercise.
Place conditioning according to the session goal and fatigue demands. This resistance-session template puts optional conditioning here; endurance-focused sessions need a different plan.
Reduce effort gradually, use comfortable mobility if desired, and record performance and recovery.

ordering.evidence_boundary: Strength adaptations can favor exercises performed early. The detailed stage template is an explicit product policy, not a learned optimal order or a direct finding for every goal.
